task: Core #1186 F6-U03h: prove historical 0046 RLS policy role-OID portability without modifying canonical guard

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical risk task on historic security-related RLS policy metadata. Evidence must be sourced from genuine 47-file historical PostgreSQL17 replay and independent read-only hosted catalog role identity, with tamper/failure cases. Only diagnostic parity can be concluded; F6-U03f live and destructive target checks remain untouched.

acceptanceCriteria: Use the exact F6-U03f catalog SQL as the source for role-name-normalized policy digest, replacing only p.polroles::text with a single deterministic role-name projection; all original SQL remains byte-identical.
Verify independent hosted reference 126 policies, 124 authenticated and 2 anon, with hosted role OIDs 16485 and 16484 respectively; local OIDs must be observed rather than prescribed.
Real 47/47 source-pinned Docker PG17 replay produces raw and stable policy MD5, and an explicit fail-closed comparison identifies whether numeric OIDs alone explain the prior mismatch.
Report only bounded local policy metadata equivalence if normalized hashes match; fail on a remaining normalized mismatch without adjusting expected fingerprints.
Preserve F6-U03b abort-before-DROP and F6-U03f full strict target guard, no hosted write nor staging/Fresh project reallocation.
Run exact-head independent Docker PG17 proof, canonical CI, Security, Truth and Lifecycle before closing this scoped diagnostic.
invariants: Only seven catalog object kinds are present, all unchanged original definition checks remain intact.
Original F6-U03f and original 47 migration SQL bytes are not edited, and 59-file source compiler remains hard-disabled before any DROP.
Stable policy projection sorts role names deterministically and fails on unmapped OIDs; it never guesses a role or changes RLS decision semantics.
All SQL tests are isolated, pinned to disposable PostgreSQL17 Docker peer, fixed local database and known fixture role.
Local normalized equality never certifies full hosted F6-U03f target guard, TLS identity, 59-file replay or signed-in tenant RLS.
forbiddenStates: Changing p.polroles::text in the canonical live guard or silently accepting a changed raw schema fingerprint.
Reporting POLICY_OID_ONLY based on matching counts or a fabricated/synthetic no-replay fixture.
Treating a missing/unknown role as PUBLIC or permissive role without fail-closed flag.
Connecting to hosted Supabase for SQL execution via CI environment or applying a destructive schema reset.
Promoting fixture to genuine Auth/Storage/event trigger and Alap/Pro runtime proof.

failureModes: Role OIDs differ as expected but policy expression text differs too, leading to a false normalized pass.
Naive substitution changes original object catalog UNION or sorts roles nondeterministically.
A role OID has no corresponding pg_roles row and COALESCE incorrectly maps it to PUBLIC.
CI local libpq environment points to an external hosted PostgreSQL target.
Source history drifts from canonical 0046 and the replay silently bypasses failed SQL.
Normalizing policy roles is incorrectly used to weaken the production target guard.
edgeCases: All 126 policy names exist, but one expression or USING clause is changed.
authenticated/anon role OIDs are equal across environments but named-role hashes still differ.
pg_policy contains a PUBLIC marker OID 0 alongside authenticated role; preserve PUBLIC marker deterministically.
Role-order variations generate different polroles arrays but equal semantic role membership; deterministic normalization makes names comparable.
One unresolvable nonzero OID cannot be mapped to a role name and must be flagged.
Local database has PG17 and exact object count, but provider-managed Auth is only stubbed.
Local migration 0026 appears twice under different names and both must be verified.
Raw catalog MD5 remains blocked due to OID even when stable policy digest matches.

alternatives.summary: Derive role-name-normalized per-policy SQL from existing F6-U03f catalog source and execute on genuine 0046 temporary PostgreSQL17, compared to independently read-only hosted reference.
alternatives.reason: Preserves production fail-closed raw fingerprint while isolating environmental OID serialization from semantic policy contents.

alternatives.reason: Would weaken production schema drift detection and conflate provider-specific security authority with local fixture semantics.

alternatives.summary: Create roles with the exact hosted OID numbers inside Docker, or edit pg_catalog so replay fingerprint matches by force.

specialistReviews.finding: A matching normalized policy digest could be misreported as the full hosted transaction guard accepting a local source replay.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep the canonical guard unchanged and require explicit local-only scope flags; tested normalized equality cannot authorize live execution or credential use.

specialistReviews.finding: pg_policy.polroles stores role OIDs which are database-local metadata; names are resolved using pg_roles but missing entries can invalidate certainty.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use sorted role-name projection with unknown-role sentinel, fail if unknown role appears, verify individual role OID summaries at both ends.

specialistReviews.finding: A generated diagnostic query can drift from the actual full canonical object_defs SQL during refactoring.
specialistReviews.resolution: Extract source from compileCatalogQueries().original and replace only the unique exact role OID textual fragment; unit test canonical query digest and no mutation.

specialistReviews.finding: One genuine local PG17 transaction alone does not prove provider-managed Supabase Auth, Storage, TLS host or newly added 0047-0058 SQL.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep owner-specific release gates and Fresh Install hosted reset BLOCKED; publish CI results only for 0046 policy role identity diagnostic.

challenge.scenario: Same policy count and role distribution but a predicate changes from tenant-private to overly permissive.
challenge.finding: Count-only check may silently pass despite a security-relevant policy expression modification.
challenge.resolution: Compare complete canonical policy definition text with exactly the OID serialization replaced; require matching MD5.

challenge.scenario: Unknown nonzero role OID is normalized to a default or PUBLIC role.
challenge.finding: Unmapped principals can be misclassified and conceal a real security policy drift.
challenge.resolution: The derived query emits a sentinel and the proof rejects any unmapped role OID before evaluating parity.

challenge.scenario: Local migration fixture passes without executing all 47 unchanged historical files.
challenge.finding: Synthetic table counts cannot attest application policy SQL parity.
challenge.resolution: Assert every historical Git blob against canonical hosted source, then transactionally apply all 47 files in Docker PG17.

challenge.scenario: The helper edits the production F6-U03f policy hash definition rather than a diagnostic SELECT.
challenge.finding: A false-positive full-guard result may pass even when the true target changed.
challenge.resolution: Derive only one separate read-only query from canonical SQL and test strict guard SHA/no code modification.

challenge.scenario: Role order changes in arrays across database clusters but membership remains the same.
challenge.finding: Direct string comparison can fail on ordering despite equivalent role membership.
challenge.resolution: Resolve and sort role names as a multiset with explicit deterministic separators; never drop duplicates silently.

challenge.scenario: Fresh Install reference MD5 changes after historical snapshot read and local fixture still marks a current pass.
challenge.finding: Snapshot mismatch does not establish live state freshness or connection identity.
challenge.resolution: Label reference date/project; require separate live target confirmation for any later action; never claim deploy READY.

challenge.scenario: PGHOSTADDR or DATABASE_URL leaks into CI, redirecting fixture replay away from Docker.
challenge.finding: A destructive historical script could act on the wrong cluster if peer selection is not pinned.
challenge.resolution: Preserve hard-coded Docker loopback/role/DB and inspect container-reported IP before any replay.

challenge.scenario: A normalized policy match is interpreted as successful authenticated tenant RLS.
challenge.finding: Metadata hash equality cannot test JWT, session claims, role grants, provider triggers and tenant scope.
challenge.resolution: Keep provider semantics and signed-in Alap/Pro RLS as explicit unresolved blockers despite local diagnostic PASS.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The genuine 47-file historical PostgreSQL17 replay reconstructs 4621 canonical catalog objects; only the 126 RLS-policy definitions differ from the real Fresh Install host, even though table counts and six other object-kind hashes match. The canonical F6-U03f raw policy catalog uses p.polroles::text, which includes cluster-dependent role OIDs, but actual divergence may include policy expression changes. We need isolated evidence separating OID serialization from real security policy differences.
observableOutcomes: An immutable query derived from the unchanged canonical F6-U03f object_defs source computes both raw and role-name-normalized per-policy fingerprints with explicit 126-policy count.

A real isolated Docker PostgreSQL17 replay executes all 47 source-authentic migrations, displays local anon/authenticated role OIDs and tests role-name-normalized MD5 against independently observed Fresh Install reference e5dc03a08c272c6b993b45306c5f664d.
A passing diagnostic distinguishes raw OID differences from actual SQL-expression or role membership differences and never authorizes a hosted reset or a full guard PASS.
Negative unit/CI cases fail on missing names, unknown policy roles, 125/127 policy counts, altered role mappings, changed policy expressions or fake local-run success.
Exact-head Plan Before Code, Development Guard, Edit-Time Guard, Resumable Replay, all Quality tests, TS, production build, Truth Gate and Lifecycle are checked.
unresolvedRisks: Role names may differ across environments in addition to numeric OIDs; an identical normalized digest must only support a bounded diagnostic inference.
Provider-managed Auth, Storage, event triggers, ACL and libpq/TLS target identity cannot be established by a disposable Docker Postgres replay.
No evidence yet proves that 59 historical+new Office SQL migrations can be safely applied to the hosted Fresh Install schema or tenant-authenticated access paths.
